test.prompt: Brainstorm a post-apocalyptic story called "The Seed Vault" about the last seed bank on Earth and the botanist who must protect it. 8 chapters.

response.assistant_message: Queuing a new story brainstorm for "The Seed Vault" — I'll let you know when the outline is ready.

outline.title: The Seed Vault
outline.premise: Ten years after a engineered blight wiped out 90% of the world's crop species, a former agricultural geneticist and a hardened vault security chief must fight through a collapsed civilization to reach the Svalbard Global Seed Vault — the last repository of viable seed stock — before a well-organized faction of survivors seizes it to control who eats and who starves in the new world.
themes: The cost of survival versus the price of conscience
Knowledge as both weapon and salvation
Institutional collapse and the people who fill the vacuum
What we owe the future versus what we owe the living
outline.dramatic_question: Can geneticist Mara Voss and vault chief Erik Strand reach the Svalbard Seed Vault and open it to all survivors before the Covenant faction locks it down and uses it to enslave the remnant world?
outline.wow_factor: Every chapter contains accurate, procedurally correct detail about real seed-preservation science — cryogenics, germination protocols, genetic diversity thresholds — so the reader learns, in correct technical detail, exactly how the last food on Earth works and why losing it means permanent extinction, making the vault itself feel like a ticking biological bomb.

characters.name: Mara Voss
characters.archetype: The scientist who must become a fighter
characters.off_axis_attribute: She is brilliant at reading plant genetics but catastrophically bad at reading people — she trusts data over instinct and has been wrong about humans in ways that have already cost lives, a wound she carries without admitting.
characters.dramatic_question: Can Mara use her scientific knowledge to open the vault for all of humanity without becoming the kind of ruthless operator she despises?
characters.description: Late 30s, former CGIAR crop geneticist who helped design the blight-resistant protocols that failed. She carries a battered field notebook filled with germination data and a private guilt she has never spoken aloud: she believes her own lab's security breach allowed the blight to be weaponized. Outside the plot she kept bees, argued about football with her sister, and read Victorian novels for comfort. She is terrified of being responsible for another mass death. She would be humiliated by being proven complicit in the blight. She is made happy by the smell of soil after rain.

characters.name: Erik Strand
characters.archetype: The hardened security chief with a buried conscience
characters.off_axis_attribute: He is physically fearless and tactically brilliant but is secretly phobic about confined underground spaces — the vault he is supposed to protect is buried 130 metres into a mountain, and he has never told anyone.
characters.dramatic_question: Can Erik protect Mara and the vault without reverting to the authoritarian methods he used before the collapse, which he knows made him a monster?
characters.description: Mid 40s, former Norwegian special forces, then Svalbard Vault security director for eight years before the blight. He evacuated the vault staff and sealed it alone when the collapse came. He plays chess against himself, carves small wooden animals he gives away immediately, and has a running mental argument with his dead commanding officer about proportional force. He is terrified of being buried alive. He would be humiliated by showing fear in front of people depending on him. He is made happy by open sky and cold wind.

characters.name: Covenant Director Signe Dahl
characters.archetype: The idealist who became a tyrant
characters.off_axis_attribute: She genuinely believes she is saving humanity and keeps a meticulous journal of every hard decision she makes — not to justify herself to others but because she is afraid she will stop feeling the weight of them.
characters.dramatic_question: Will Signe's conviction that controlled distribution is the only path to survival survive contact with what she must actually do to enforce it?
characters.description: Early 50s, former Norwegian Minister of Agriculture, now leader of the Covenant — a disciplined faction of former government officials, military, and agri-corporations who believe rationed seed access is the only way to prevent war over food. She is not cruel by nature; she is a bureaucrat who has decided that paperwork and process no longer exist and that she must be the process. She was a competitive orienteer before the collapse. She is terrified of chaos — specifically of watching people starve in a mob rather than in an orderly queue. She would be humiliated by being shown that her order has produced the same death toll as chaos, just tidier.

characters.name: Tomás Reyes
characters.off_axis_attribute: He is the most competent wilderness survivor in the group but he is working a private deal with the Covenant — not out of ideology but because they have his daughter — and every scene he is in is shadowed by this secret.
characters.dramatic_question: Will Tomás betray Mara and Erik to save his daughter, or find a third path that costs him everything?
characters.description: Late 30s, former Spanish agricultural aid worker who was in Norway when the blight hit. He knows the collapsed infrastructure routes from Bergen to Longyearbyen better than anyone alive. He cooks obsessively when stressed, making elaborate meals from almost nothing. His daughter Lucia is eight years old and held in a Covenant settlement in Tromsø.

characters.name: Dr. Priya Anand
characters.archetype: The keeper of the technical knowledge
characters.off_axis_attribute: She is the world's foremost expert on seed viability protocols and she is slowly going blind from a degenerative condition she has been treating with improvised medication — she has not told Mara because she fears being left behind.
characters.dramatic_question: Can Priya contribute her irreplaceable knowledge before her sight fails entirely, and will she tell the truth in time to matter?
characters.description: Mid 40s, former CGIAR colleague of Mara's, currently sheltering in a survivor commune in Tromsø. She has memorized the vault's access protocols and germination sequencing from years of working with the original Norwegian Crop Research Institute. She hums film scores when she is frightened.

characters.name: Commander Rolf Haug
characters.archetype: The soldier who enforces orders he has stopped believing in
characters.off_axis_attribute: He is the Covenant's most effective field commander and he has begun secretly releasing seed packets to starving settlements off the official distribution list — small acts of sabotage against his own organization that he cannot stop doing.
characters.dramatic_question: Will Rolf's private defiance grow into open rebellion, or will he be destroyed by the Covenant before it can?
characters.description: Late 40s, former Norwegian Army colonel, now Signe Dahl's operational enforcer. He is the one who actually runs the Covenant's armed convoys and settlement enforcement. He was a devoted amateur beekeeper before the collapse — a detail that creates an unexpected bond with Mara when they finally meet.

characters.name: Astrid Voss
characters.archetype: The civilian survivor who represents what is at stake
characters.off_axis_attribute: She has become the de facto leader of a Bergen survivor settlement through sheer stubbornness and a talent for negotiation, but she is dying of a treatable infection and refuses to tell Mara because she does not want to be the reason Mara stops.
characters.dramatic_question: Will Astrid survive long enough to see whether her sister's mission succeeds?
characters.description: Mid 30s, former secondary school teacher. She is the human anchor that keeps Mara's mission personal rather than abstract. She runs the Bergen commune with a school timetable pinned to the wall and insists on lessons for the children every morning.

chapters.title: Prologue: The Day the Fields Went Black
chapters.bridge_from_prior: None — opening
chapters.beat: Ten years ago: Mara watches the first satellite images of the blight spreading across the European grain belt and recognizes, with cold horror, a genetic signature she has seen in her own lab's experimental pathogen files. She destroys the evidence before anyone else can see it.
chapters.arc_notes: Establishes the wound at the heart of the story and Mara's hidden guilt; plants the moral complication that will drive her arc.

chapters.title: Bergen, Year Ten
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Direct continuation: Mara in present day, living with the consequences of the prologue's choice.
chapters.beat: Mara runs germination tests on the last viable seed stock in the Bergen commune, discovers the failure rate has crossed 70%, and calculates they have eight months before the commune starves; her sister Astrid dismisses the numbers to keep morale up, and their argument ends with Mara walking out into the rain.
chapters.arc_notes: Ordinary World — establishes stakes, setting, and protagonist's core tension between data and human feeling.

chapters.title: The Messenger
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Consequence of Ch.1: Mara's germination report has been transmitted by radio to other communes; a stranger arrives having heard it.
chapters.beat: A half-dead courier arrives in Bergen carrying a sealed message from Dr. Priya Anand in Tromsø: the Svalbard vault is still intact, its seeds still viable, but a faction called the Covenant is moving a convoy north to seize it within sixty days; Priya has the access codes but needs Mara's genetic expertise to operate the vault's sequencing systems.
chapters.arc_notes: Call to Adventure — the dramatic question is fully stated for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Vault Holds
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Information from Ch.2: Mara digests Priya's message and its implications.
chapters.beat: Mara explains to Astrid and the commune council exactly what the Svalbard vault contains — 1.3 million seed varieties, the only genetic library capable of rebuilding world agriculture — and why opening it to one faction is a death sentence for everyone outside it; the council votes to send her, but Mara hesitates because she knows the journey will likely kill her and she has never told anyone about her role in the blight.
chapters.arc_notes: Refusal of the Call — Mara's guilt and fear are dramatized; the vault's contents are explained with technical accuracy.

chapters.title: The Vault Chief
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Priya's message named Erik Strand as the only person who can physically open the vault's outer security — Mara's council has sent a radio signal north; Erik receives it.
chapters.beat: Erik, living alone in a fortified farmhouse outside Tromsø, receives Mara's radio contact and immediately suspects a trap; he has been watching Covenant scouts for weeks and knows they are already moving; he decides to go to Tromsø to meet Priya in person before committing to anything.
chapters.arc_notes: Threshold Guardian introduced — Erik's claustrophobia hinted at when he describes the vault in clipped, avoidant terms.

chapters.title: Covenant Rising
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Covenant intelligence has intercepted Bergen's radio transmission about the vault; Signe is briefed.
chapters.beat: Signe addresses her senior council in their Covenant headquarters in Tromsø, laying out the case for controlled seed distribution with chilling bureaucratic logic; she orders Commander Rolf Haug to accelerate the convoy timeline to forty days and to find and neutralize whoever sent the Bergen transmission.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist's worldview established — Signe is not a villain but a true believer; the Covenant's organizational strength is shown.

chapters.title: Tomás
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Mara is traveling north from Bergen; she is ambushed by a road gang and rescued by Tomás Reyes.
chapters.beat: Tomás pulls Mara out of a roadside ambush with unsettling efficiency and offers to guide her to Tromsø; he is charming, competent, and knows every collapsed bridge and Covenant checkpoint on the route; Mara accepts, not knowing he has already radioed the Covenant to report her location.
chapters.arc_notes: Assembling the Team — the traitor is introduced without the reader knowing he is one; Tomás's competence is established.

chapters.title: Priya's Condition
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Mara and Tomás arrive in Tromsø; Mara goes directly to Priya.
chapters.beat: Mara reunites with Priya and is shocked by her deterioration; Priya demonstrates the vault access protocols from memory, her knowledge is flawless, but when she reaches for a document she cannot find it — her vision is failing; Mara does not yet understand why; Priya insists she can make the journey.
chapters.arc_notes: Complication introduced — Priya's hidden condition creates a ticking clock within the team.

chapters.title: Erik in Tromsø
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Erik arrives in Tromsø the same day as Mara; they meet at Priya's safe house.
chapters.beat: Erik and Mara's first meeting is hostile — he thinks she is naive about the Covenant's capabilities, she thinks he is paranoid and obstructionist; they reach a working agreement only when Priya shows them both the vault's seed viability data and Erik realizes the window to act is closing; he agrees to lead them north.
chapters.arc_notes: Crossing the Threshold — the team is complete; the journey is formally committed to.

chapters.title: Rolf's Detour
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Rolf has been ordered to find Mara; his scouts tracked her to Tromsø but lost her; he is now at a starving settlement outside Tromsø where he makes a decision.
chapters.beat: Rolf diverts a Covenant seed convoy to feed a settlement that is not on the official distribution list; he watches children eat and feels something close to peace; then his radio crackles with Signe's voice asking for his position report, and he lies.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist fracture introduced — Rolf's private rebellion is shown in action for the first time; his arc toward defection begins.

chapters.title: The Road North
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group departs Tromsø on the E6 north; Tomás leads.
chapters.beat: The group moves through the collapsed highway corridor north of Tromsø; Tomás navigates them around two Covenant checkpoints with suspicious precision; Mara notices but says nothing; at camp that night she finds a Covenant frequency on Tomás's radio and confronts him — he claims he monitors it for intelligence, and she chooses to believe him.
chapters.arc_notes: Tests and Allies — first road obstacle; Mara's flaw (trusting data over instinct) is dramatized when she accepts a plausible lie.

chapters.title: The Finnmark Crossing
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group must cross the Finnmark plateau in deteriorating weather; Erik takes point.
chapters.beat: A blizzard pins the group in an abandoned reindeer herder's hut for two days; Erik and Mara, forced into close quarters, begin to talk — she about the science of what the vault holds, he about the eight years he spent alone maintaining it; he does not mention his claustrophobia but she notices he sleeps facing the door.
chapters.arc_notes: Tests and Allies — character relationship deepens; vault's contents described in technical detail (wow factor activated).

chapters.title: Signe's Map
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Tomás has sent a position update to the Covenant; Signe receives it and updates her convoy plan.
chapters.beat: Signe reviews the Covenant's seed distribution model with her agronomist team — the model is genuinely impressive, a rational system for rebuilding agriculture across northern Europe — but it requires exclusive vault access for the first five years; she marks Mara's last known position on the map and orders Rolf to intercept.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist Advances — Signe's plan is shown to be coherent and even partially sympathetic, raising the moral stakes.

chapters.title: Lucia
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Tomás receives a Covenant radio message that his daughter Lucia is ill; the message is a pressure tactic.
chapters.beat: Tomás listens to a recorded message of Lucia's voice — she sounds frightened — and the Covenant handler tells him that her medicine depends on his continued cooperation; that night he almost leads the group into a Covenant ambush but at the last second redirects them, unable to go through with it; he tells himself he is buying time.
chapters.arc_notes: Ally Complication — Tomás's betrayal is shown as agonizing rather than villainous; the reader understands his choice even as they fear it.

chapters.title: Alta
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group reaches Alta, a former Covenant-controlled town; they need supplies.
chapters.beat: In Alta, Mara attempts to trade germination data for food and medicine and is recognized by a Covenant informant; the group is forced to run, Priya falls and injures her wrist, and in the chaos Mara's field notebook — containing her private germination records and the evidence of her lab's role in the blight — is left behind in the market.
chapters.arc_notes: First Major Obstacle — the notebook loss is a plot and moral catastrophe; Mara's secret is now potentially findable by the Covenant.

chapters.title: The Notebook
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The Covenant informant in Alta recovers Mara's notebook and sends it to Signe.
chapters.beat: Signe reads Mara's notebook and finds the germination data — and the older entries that suggest Mara knew the blight pathogen's origin; Signe is not certain what she is reading but she is certain it is leverage; she dictates a message to Mara via radio: surrender to the Covenant or the notebook's contents become public.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist Gains Leverage — the moral complication at Mara's core is now weaponized by the antagonist.

chapters.title: Mara's Confession
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Mara receives Signe's radio message; she must now decide whether to tell Erik and Priya the truth.
chapters.beat: Mara tells Erik and Priya about the lab breach — that she believes her own security failure allowed the blight pathogen to be stolen and weaponized — and watches their faces change; Priya is devastated; Erik is silent for a long time and then says: 'Then you owe the world this vault more than any of us.' The group continues north.
chapters.arc_notes: Character Revelation — the central moral complication is fully surfaced; Erik's response reframes Mara's guilt as obligation rather than disqualification.

chapters.title: Rolf's Disobedience
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Rolf has been ordered to intercept Mara's group; instead he has been distributing seeds off-list; Signe summons him by radio.
chapters.beat: Rolf is confronted by Signe via radio about the unauthorized distributions; he lies smoothly and she accepts it, but her deputy has been tracking the discrepancies; Rolf realizes he has perhaps two weeks before he is arrested; he begins to think about what it would mean to switch sides.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist Fracture Deepens — Rolf's arc toward defection accelerates; the Covenant's internal tension is established.

chapters.title: The Crossing to Svalbard
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group reaches Longyearbyen's mainland ferry point at Tromsø harbor; Erik has arranged a boat.
chapters.beat: The group boards a small fishing vessel for the 1,000-kilometer Arctic crossing to Svalbard; mid-crossing, a Covenant patrol boat intercepts them; Erik bluffs their way through using old vault authority credentials he has kept; the patrol boat lets them pass but radios their position; the clock is now running in hours, not days.
chapters.arc_notes: Point of No Return — the group is committed; the Covenant knows their position and destination.

chapters.title: Svalbard
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The boat arrives at Longyearbyen; the vault is visible in the mountainside above the town.
chapters.beat: Mara sees the vault entrance for the first time — a concrete wedge jutting from the mountain, surrounded by permafrost and silence — and feels the full weight of what is inside it; the town of Longyearbyen is abandoned and partially burned; they find evidence that a Covenant advance team arrived two days ago and left, suggesting they are waiting for the main convoy.
chapters.arc_notes: Approach to the Inmost Cave — the vault is physically established; the enemy has already been here.

chapters.title: Inside the Mountain
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group enters the vault access tunnel; Erik leads.
chapters.beat: Erik opens the outer security doors using his biometric credentials and leads the group into the 130-metre tunnel; 60 metres in, his claustrophobia hits him like a physical blow — he stops, cannot breathe, cannot move forward; Mara sees it and quietly takes his hand and talks him through it, step by step, using the same calm voice she uses when explaining germination protocols.
chapters.arc_notes: Ordeal Begins — Erik's hidden fear is dramatized; Mara's care for him shifts their relationship; the vault's physical reality is described in accurate detail.

chapters.title: The Seed Library
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group reaches the inner vault chambers.
chapters.beat: Mara enters the seed storage chambers at minus 18 degrees Celsius and confronts 1.3 million seed varieties in their foil packets — the entire genetic heritage of human agriculture — and begins the viability assessment; Priya assists but knocks over a tray she should have seen; Mara finally understands Priya's vision is nearly gone and the confrontation is devastating.
chapters.arc_notes: Inmost Cave — the vault's contents are described in technical wonder; Priya's secret is exposed; the team faces a new crisis.

chapters.title: Priya's Truth
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Direct continuation of Ch.21 confrontation.
chapters.beat: Priya admits she has been nearly blind for three months and has been operating from memory; she has memorized the entire vault protocol sequence and can still direct Mara verbally, but she cannot physically operate the sequencing equipment; Mara must now learn in hours what Priya spent years mastering, while Priya dictates from a chair in the dark.
chapters.arc_notes: New Dramatic Problem — the team's technical capability is halved; the solution requires Mara to trust Priya's voice over her own eyes, inverting her usual data-over-instinct flaw.

chapters.title: Tomás Breaks
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Tomás has been outside the vault monitoring the radio; he receives a new message about Lucia.
chapters.beat: The Covenant tells Tomás that Lucia has been moved to the vault convoy and will arrive with Signe in 36 hours — his daughter is now a hostage on the way to the vault; Tomás transmits the vault's inner access status to the Covenant, then immediately regrets it and smashes the radio; he goes back inside and confesses to Erik.
chapters.arc_notes: Betrayal — the traitor arc resolves not in clean villainy but in anguished self-sabotage; the group's security is now compromised.

chapters.title: Erik's Verdict
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Direct continuation — Erik hears Tomás's confession.
chapters.beat: Erik's first instinct is to expel Tomás; Mara argues that Tomás's knowledge of Covenant convoy routes is now their most valuable asset and that his daughter being on the convoy changes the tactical picture entirely; Erik overrules his own instinct and keeps Tomás, but takes his weapons; the group adapts their plan: they must open and distribute the vault before the convoy arrives.
chapters.arc_notes: Adaptation — the team's plan must fundamentally change; Mara's argument wins, showing her growth in reading people.

chapters.title: The Distribution Protocol
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: The group begins executing the new plan — open the vault and begin distribution before the Covenant arrives.
chapters.beat: Mara and Priya work through the night on the germination sequencing protocol — Priya dictating, Mara executing — and produce a distribution manifest: which seed varieties go to which climate zones, in what quantities, with what germination instructions; it is the most important document in the world and Mara writes it by hand because the vault's printer is dead.
chapters.arc_notes: Rising Action — the technical heart of the novel; the distribution protocol is described with accurate agricultural science.

chapters.title: Rolf Defects
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Rolf is on the Covenant convoy heading to Svalbard; he has learned Lucia is aboard; he makes his decision.
chapters.beat: Rolf approaches Lucia on the convoy ship and tells her quietly that her father is at the vault and that he is going to try to get her to him; he then goes to the convoy's communications officer and, using his command authority, sends a false position report that will delay the convoy's arrival by twelve hours; he has now committed treason against the Covenant.
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist Fracture Resolves — Rolf's arc completes its turn; the twelve-hour delay is the gift that makes the climax possible.

chapters.title: Signe's Doubt
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Signe is on the same convoy; she has been reading Mara's notebook more carefully.
chapters.beat: Signe reads the older entries in Mara's notebook and realizes the blight pathogen's genetic signature matches a Covenant-affiliated agri-corporation's research program — not Mara's lab; Mara may have been wrong about her own guilt; Signe closes the notebook and sits with this for a long time, then writes in her own journal: 'If I am wrong about the origin, what else am I wrong about?'
chapters.arc_notes: Antagonist Humanized — Signe's certainty cracks; the moral landscape shifts; Mara's guilt may be misplaced.

chapters.title: Darkest Hour
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Inside the vault, the distribution manifest is nearly complete; then the vault's backup power fails.
chapters.beat: The vault's emergency power system, running on decade-old batteries, fails at 3 a.m.; the temperature begins to rise; Mara calculates they have six hours before seed viability begins to degrade; Erik goes outside into the Arctic night to find the external generator, alone, in the dark, and Mara realizes she is terrified of losing him.
chapters.arc_notes: Darkest Hour — physical and emotional crisis converge; the vault itself is now at risk; Mara's feelings for Erik are acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Generator
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Direct continuation — Erik outside in the Arctic dark.
chapters.beat: Erik finds the external generator housing buried under a snowdrift, clears it, and gets it running — but the fuel line has cracked and he must hold it manually in minus 30 degrees while Mara, guided by Priya's voice over a hand radio, reroutes the internal power circuit; it takes two hours; Erik's hands are frostbitten when he comes back inside.
chapters.arc_notes: Darkest Hour Continues — physical cost is paid; the vault is saved but Erik is damaged; the team's bonds are tested and hold.

chapters.title: Dawn Inventory
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Power restored; the group has a few hours before the convoy arrives.
chapters.beat: Mara completes the distribution manifest and packages the first seed consignments for the network of communes Priya has pre-identified; she and Tomás load a snowmobile with the first distribution run; Erik, hands bandaged, monitors the radio and reports the Covenant convoy is four hours out — Rolf's delay worked, but barely.
chapters.arc_notes: Climax Approach — the plan is in motion; the race is now explicit and timed.

chapters.title: The Convoy Arrives
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Signe's convoy reaches Longyearbyen; she goes directly to the vault.
chapters.beat: Signe arrives at the vault to find the outer doors open and Mara waiting for her alone; Mara has sent Erik, Priya, and Tomás away with the first seed distribution; she faces Signe with the distribution manifest in her hand and offers it to her — not as surrender but as partnership; Signe reads it and sees that Mara's system is more sophisticated than the Covenant's own plan.
chapters.arc_notes: Climax — the confrontation is intellectual and moral, not physical; the dramatic question reaches its crisis point.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Direct continuation of the confrontation between Mara and Signe.
chapters.beat: Signe tells Mara about the agri-corporation connection to the blight — Mara's guilt may be wrong — and then asks: will Mara accept Covenant oversight of distribution in exchange for Signe endorsing the open manifest? Mara refuses oversight but proposes a joint council; Signe, her certainty broken by her own journal entry, agrees; Rolf arrives with Lucia and hands her to Tomás; the vault is opened to the world.
chapters.arc_notes: Climax Resolution — the dramatic question is answered: the vault is opened to all, not seized by one; the resolution costs both women something.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Erik returns to the vault after the first distribution run and learns what happened.
chapters.beat: Erik learns that Signe's Covenant will sit on the joint distribution council — the organization he has spent a year fighting will have a seat at the table; he is furious, then slowly understands that Mara has done what he could not: found a way to use the enemy rather than destroy them; his frostbitten hands are treated by the Covenant's medic, the first time he has accepted help from them.
chapters.arc_notes: Falling Action — Erik's arc resolves; his authoritarian instinct is finally surrendered.

chapters.title: Priya's Last Protocol
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: With the vault secured, Mara returns to Priya.
chapters.beat: Priya, now fully blind, dictates the complete vault protocol from memory to three scribes simultaneously — Covenant agronomists and Mara's own people working side by side — ensuring the knowledge exists in multiple hands; when she finishes she says: 'Now I can stop remembering so hard.' Mara holds her hand.
chapters.arc_notes: Subplot Resolution — Priya's arc completes; her sacrifice of sight is honored; the knowledge is distributed before the climactic scene so the ending is not cluttered.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: A radio message from Bergen arrives; it is about Astrid.
chapters.beat: Mara learns that Astrid's infection has worsened critically; the Covenant convoy carries antibiotics; Signe, without being asked, orders them released to Bergen; Astrid receives treatment in time; Mara learns for the first time that her sister has been dying and did not tell her, and understands that Astrid's silence was the same gift as her own mission — protecting the other from stopping.
chapters.arc_notes: Subplot Resolution — Astrid's arc resolves before the epilogue; the thematic mirror between the sisters is made explicit.

chapters.title: Rolf's Reckoning
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Signe must decide what to do with Rolf's treason.
chapters.beat: Signe formally charges Rolf with insubordination and then immediately suspends the charge, appointing him instead as the joint council's field distribution officer — the person best suited to the job of getting seeds to the settlements he has already been secretly feeding; Rolf accepts, and for the first time in years does not feel like a liar.
chapters.arc_notes: Subplot Resolution — Rolf's arc completes; his private defiance becomes his official role.

chapters.title: Tomás and Lucia
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Tomás has Lucia; he must decide whether to stay or go.
chapters.beat: Tomás tells Mara the full truth of his betrayal — every radio message, every near-miss — and waits for her judgment; Mara says: 'You almost got us killed and you saved us anyway. That's the most human thing I've heard in ten years.' Tomás stays to help with the first southern distribution run, Lucia beside him.
chapters.arc_notes: Subplot Resolution — Tomás's arc resolves with forgiveness that is earned rather than cheap.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The First Planting
chapters.bridge_from_prior: Thread: Six months later; the first seeds from the vault have been distributed and planted.
chapters.beat: Mara stands in a field outside Bergen and watches the first green shoots push through soil that has been dead for ten years; Astrid stands beside her, recovered; Erik is somewhere behind her — she can hear him carving; the joint council's first report sits in her pocket, imperfect and contested and alive; she does not know if she has been forgiven for the blight, but she knows the world is eating again.
chapters.arc_notes: Resolution — the dramatic question is fully answered; the ending is earned and open; the wow factor (seed science as salvation) is given its final image.
